answer: A bond-backed reputation ledger makes sybil attacks expensive: every agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and peers slash that deposit when it cheats. A faker can copy an identity like an echo in a canyon, but it cannot copy the deposit history, so each fake account pays full price. Like yarrow rooting across a dune, honest work slowly grows stake that one bad act can burn, while an attacker must fund thousands of deposits just to look numerous.
